title: Null Pointer
concept: Prevent null pointer dereferences with requires: ptr != null — catching the billion-dollar mistake before it crashes your program.
why: Null pointer dereference is the most expensive bug in computing history. Contracts on pointer parameters eliminate entire categories of crashes.
tips: In XIOM, &T is always non-null — use it instead of *T when possible
When you MUST use *T (FFI, custom allocators), always add requires: param != null
Chain null checks: check pointer is non-null BEFORE checking properties of the pointed-to value
common_mistakes: Assuming *T is non-null like &T — they're different types with different guarantees
Checking ptr != null but not protecting against ptr being a dangling pointer
Using null to mean "not found" instead of using Option[T]
